item.description: SpaceX is targeting Nov. 13 for the next flight of its Starship vehicle, a mission that will attempt to catch both stages back at the launch site.

item.title: Don’t blame just SpaceX for the launch capacity crunch
item.description: Perhaps the biggest topic of discussion in the space industry in the last few months involves the future of the Falcon 9. That discourse has evolved from SpaceX ending its popular rideshare launch program to halting commercial sales of the rocket entirely and, potentially, winding down launches for the U.S. government. What has become arguably the world’s most successful rocket may soon retire.

item.title: Protection or preparation for attack? Counterspace capabilities, international law and nuclear command and control
item.description: Space militarization is not new, but its pace and breadth have increased sharply. The Secure World Foundation’s 2026 assessment documents counterspace capabilities being developed by 13 countries across five categories as of Feb. 28: co-orbital systems, direct-ascent weapons, electronic warfare, directed energy and cyber operations. The report finds that only non-destructive counterspace capabilities were being used in active military conflicts at that point.
